title: Summary: adding a blinking rear-sonar ATTENTION warning to the ACT LCD

parts: You are Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude. You are an interactive agent that helps users with software engineering tasks in the project at C:/Users/victo/Desktop/nxp project (NXP summer school autonomous vehicle: MCXA153 VCU hub plus two Arduinos and an ESP32 gateway, linked over UART and I2C).

lets add a feature: we have the feature for front sensor. for the rear one, if there is also something near him, it should send a message of "ATTENTION" to be displayed to lcd. dont change anything else

Compiles clean and links, no warnings.

## What I added

All of it lives in the VCU (led_blinky.c) - that's the only node that both hears `P,<front>,<back>,<pir>` from PERC and can send `M,<text>` to ACT's display.

**Thresholds** (led_blinky.c:139) - `REAR_ALERT_CM 25` matches the front guard's `GUARD_STOP_CM`. `REAR_CLEAR_CM 32` is the release point: a wall sitting exactly on one threshold pings 24/26/24 and a single threshold would rewrite the LCD several times a second.

**`rear_close()`** - same permissive reading as `teleop_guard()`: PERC silent -> no alert, `-1` (no echo) -> no alert.

**`rear_service()`** - edge-triggered `M,ATTENTION` on entry, and on exit it puts back whatever was on row 0 before. It re-sends once a second while the warning stands, because `M,` is fire-and-forget over SoftwareSerial with no ack and one dropped line would mean no warning at all. ACT's `lcdRow` pads instead of calling `lcd.clear()`, so the repeat doesn't flicker.

**`vcu_consume`** - the browser's `M,` text is now remembered in `s_lcdMsg`, and held rather than painted while ATTENTION owns row 0 (it would be erased by the next repeat a fraction of a second later anyway). The console says `(held - rear ATTENTION)` so it's not a mystery.

## What I deliberately did not touch

- **Drive behaviour is unchanged.** The rear sonar vetoes nothing - there's no reverse gear to veto, so this is purely a message.
- **The `T,` telemetry line** - adding a field would have meant changing the ESP32 gateway's parser too.
- **Docs** (`FIRMWARE.md`, `PROTOTYPE_1.md`, `FULL_SCHEMA.md`) - say the word and I'll add the rear alert to the protocol tables.

The `DRIVE_DUTY_MAX 70->100` and `THROTTLE_MAX 65->90` hunks in `git diff` are your own uncommitted changes from before this session, not mine.

Console output when it fires:

```
  [rear] ATTENTION (18 cm)
  [rear] clear (34 cm)
```

i want the attention message to appear and disappear constantly when something is behind to get attention. after there is a space created the lcd should stay blank until a new message to display arrives

Builds clean, `.bin` and `.elf` are current.

## What changed

**`rear_service()`** now toggles row 0 between `M,ATTENTION` and `M,` (empty) every `REAR_BLINK_MS` - 500 ms on, 500 ms off, so it flashes twice a second the whole time something is behind. `REAR_REPEAT_MS` is gone; the blink *is* the repeat, and it's self-healing: a dropped line slips the phase by one half-cycle and the next toggle resyncs it.

**On clear**, it sends one `M,` and then stops sending entirely - the `if (!s_rearAlert) return;` before the timer. Row 0 stays blank until something has a message for it.

**Reverted my restore machinery.** `s_lcdMsg` and the hold-the-browser-message logic are gone, and `vcu_consume`'s `M,` handler is byte-identical to what it was before I touched it - straight pass-through, no state. It doesn't appear in the diff at all now. The VCU is back to having no opinion about text.

ACT needed nothing: `messageSet("")` gives `g_msgLen = 0`, and `lcdRow` space-pads to 16 columns, so an empty `M,` blanks the row without a `lcd.clear()` flicker.

Two things worth knowing:

- **A browser message sent mid-alert will flash-fight the blink** - it reaches the LCD and the next toggle overwrites it within 500 ms. I left it that way deliberately: the alert outranks the text, and the blink continuing tells you so. Say the word if you'd rather the VCU swallow `M,` lines while alerting.
- **ACT's USB console prints `[lcd]` twice a second** while the alert runs, because `messageSet` logs every call. Silencing it means editing `act.ino`, which you asked me to leave alone.

The `DRIVE_DUTY_MAX` and `THROTTLE_MAX` hunks in `git diff` are still your own pre-existing uncommitted changes, untouched.
